deities: Budhanath / Bal Vriddheshwarnath - Swayambhu Shiva lingam

history.dynasty: Legendary (Treta Yuga per tradition); no ruling-dynasty attribution found
history.period: Legendary origin in the Treta Yuga; current structure about 200 years old (imagery/statues dated circa 1937)
history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple at Jogsar (Adampur), Bhagalpur, on the banks of the Uttarvahini (northward-flowing) Ganges. The Shiva lingam is believed to be Swayambhu (self-manifested), consecrated by Sage Vashishtha in the Treta Yuga during his journey with Rama and Lakshmana after the slaying of Tadka at Buxar; it remained underground until rediscovered by Mahant Balwanand Giri about 200 years ago. The deity is named Bal Vridheshwarnath in the Shiva Purana and is counted among the 108 Nath temples of India. The complex (about 3 acres, local Nagara style) includes shrines of Parvati, Durga, Radha-Krishna, Hanuman and a special Maa Bhavani shrine whose idol is believed to have floated down from Munger; the Durga idol is regarded as the Kuldevi of King Karna of Anga. Freedom fighter Tilka Manjhi worshipped here. Origins are legend-based; no archaeological dating confirmed.

name: Budhanath Temple
town_description: Bhagalpur, the 'Silk City' of Bihar, sits on the southern bank of the Ganges and is one of the oldest cities of the Gangetic plain - ancient Champa/Champanagar was the capital of the Anga Mahajanapada. It is famous for its tussar silk industry, the Vikramshila Mahavihara ruins at Antichak nearby, and as the home of Tilka Manjhi, an early tribal freedom fighter.

travel.airport: Deoghar Airport (DGH) - about 70 km (verify); Bhagalpur airport is non-operational.
travel.road: NH-80; the temple is on the banks of the Ganga at Jogsar, Adampur, Bhagalpur.

visitor_information.best_time: Shravan month (July-August) and Maha Shivratri are the biggest draws; otherwise October to March.
